# Final Experiment Design — JaxMARL PPO vs Q-Learning on SMAX (Training Time & Normalized Score)

> **Status.** Design-only. No experiment has been executed. All runtime expectations are *projected ranges*, explicitly unverified.
>
> **Locked decisions (from researcher, per U1–U9).** MAPPO primary PPO arm; IPPO ablation only. QMIX primary Q-Learning arm; VDN and IQL ablations only; no C/WQMIX. **5 seeds headline, 3 absolute floor for any run that times out (which runs must be declared)**. **One machine per campaign, one JAX backend (GPU if available, else CPU); 24 vCPU visible; per-run metadata reports backend + device count**. **2×10⁶ env steps headline; optional 5×10⁶ extension on the harder map(s) only if smoke test shows no plateau by 2×10⁶**. **Time-to-threshold at normalized score ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8} of expert; primary metric at 0.8**. **QMIX mixer hypernetwork accesses SMAX global state as in standard QMIX; asymmetry disclosed; mixer-with-state ablated vs mixer-with-only-local-state is an *optional* secondary ablation, only if space allows**. **Pinned JaxMARL released configs `algorithms/smax/{ippo,mappo,qmix,vdn,iql}` verbatim; deviations logged in a per-run overrides table**. **One learning-curve figure per map per metric, one aggregate results table per metric, one summary paragraph; Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap-CI on per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX), Holm-Bonferroni across the metric family**.

---

## 1. Rationale

JaxMARL (Rutherford et al., 2024) consolidates environment and algorithm implementations behind a single JAX stack and showcases SMAX, a JIT-friendly reimplementation of SMAC. The paper's central pitch is that JAX's JIT/XLA compilation + device parallelism make typical MARL pipelines much faster wall-clock-for-wall-clock than per-agent Python loops.

Two of the most-deployed MARL algorithm families in JaxMARL are PPO (on-policy; MAPPO/IPPO) and value-decomposition Q-Learning (off-policy; QMIX/VDN/IQL). Their reported scores on SMAX are roughly comparable at asymptotic evaluation, but their convergence profiles and amortized per-step cost are *different in kind*: on-policy rollouts + parallel advantage estimation vs. off-policy replay + target networks + periodic hard updates. We therefore ask a methodologically focused question — at equal network capacity, equal env-step budget, equal eval protocol, and a single hardware/backend, **how do the two families compare on training time and on normalized score?**

This design fixes the comparison surface area (architecture, MAPPO-vs-QMIX as head-to-head, IPPO/VDN/IQL as family-context ablations) so any observed gap can be attributed with reasonable confidence to (a) the algorithmic family, (b) the credit-assignment mechanism inside Q-Learning, (c) the centralized critic inside PPO, (d) recurrence, and (e) the QMIX global-state conditioning.

---

## 2. Hypotheses

- **H1 (final normalized score).** On SMAX, the JaxMARL headline configuration of **MAPPO** and **QMIX** reach statistically indistinguishable asymptotic normalized score at equal env-step budget.
- **H2 (training time to threshold).** **QMIX** reaches 0.8·*score_expert* in **less wall-clock time** than **MAPPO** on at least one of {3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m} at equal network and env-step budget, on the chosen JAX backend.
- **H3 (training steps to threshold, hardware-portable).** QMIX reaches 0.8·*score_expert* in **fewer environment steps** than MAPPO on {3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m}, even if H2's wall-clock direction is reversed on CPU-only backends.
- **H4 (centralized-critic contribution, PPO family).** Switching IPPO→MAPPO yields a positive normalized-score delta and a (possibly smaller) wall-clock-time-to-threshold delta on the harder maps.
- **H5 (credit-assignment contribution, Q-Learning family).** VDN outperforms IQL in final score and steps-to-threshold; QMIX outperforms VDN on the harder maps (the strong-form "QMIX ≈ +VDN+monotonic-mixer+state" claim is treated as the ablation goal, not a hypothesis).
- **H6 (recurrence).** Enabling a GRU encoder in *both* arms shifts both the final-score distribution and the wall-clock regime in a *direction-dependent* way (better sample efficiency, lower per-step throughput), with the net wall-clock-to-threshold direction left open.

We additionally pre-register **two null hypotheses** (H0-A: no head-to-head score difference at α=0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni across metrics; H0-B: no head-to-head wall-clock-to-threshold difference at α=0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni) to keep the analysis symmetrical regardless of direction.

---

## 3. Hypotheses ↔ Metrics mapping

| ID | Hypothesis | Primary metric | Secondary metric | Reporting unit |
|----|-----------|----------------|------------------|----------------|
| H1 | Final score parity | Final normalized score (mean over last 100 eval episodes) | AUC of normalized score vs env-step | per map, then aggregate |
| H2 | Wall-clock speed-up (QMIX > MAPPO) | Wall-clock seconds to first reach 0.8·*score_expert* | Wall-clock to 0.6· and 0.7· (sensitivity) | per map |
| H3 | Sample efficiency (QMIX > MAPPO) | Env steps to first reach 0.8·*score_expert* | Env steps to 0.6· and 0.7· | per map |
| H4 | Centralized critic helps PPO | Final normalized score (IPPO→MAPPO Δ) | Wall-clock & steps to 0.8· | per map |
| H5 | Credit assignment helps Q-Learning | Final normalized score across {IQL, VDN, QMIX} | Steps to 0.8· | per map |
| H6 | Recurrence | Wall-clock-to-threshold + per-step wall-clock, both arms | Final score | per map |
| H0-A | No head-to-head score difference | Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX) | — | pooled across maps |
| H0-B | No head-to-head wall-clock difference | Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-seed wall-clock deltas (PPO − QMIX) | — | pooled across maps |

**Notation reminder.** "PPO" in §7's headline comparison stands for **MAPPO**; "QMIX" stands for **QMIX**. Per-seed delta is `(headline run under arm A on seed s, map m) − (headline run under arm B on seed s, map m)`.

---

## 4. Environment & algorithm setup

### 4.1 SMAX maps
- **3m** — homogeneous, symmetric, small. Lower-difficulty baseline; both algorithms should saturate.
- **3s_vs_5z** — heterogeneous unit types *and* asymmetric team sizes; standard stress-test for credit assignment.
- **5m_vs_6m** — asymmetric team sizes; converging on this map has historically required careful hyperparameters.

Reasoning locked per U5: the *headline* budget is the same on all three maps. The **optional extension to 5×10⁶ env steps** is permitted (and *only* permitted) on **3s_vs_5z** and **5m_vs_6m**, gated on a documented smoke test that the 2×10⁶ curve has not plateaued within the last 20% of training at sub-threshold score.

### 4.2 Algorithms
| Algorithm | Role | Family | Critic/value mechanism |
|-----------|------|--------|------------------------|
| **MAPPO** | primary PPO | PPO | Centralized value V(s,𝜏), shared parameters |
| IPPO | PPO-family ablation | PPO | Independent value V_i(o_i) |
| **QMIX** | primary Q-Learning | Off-policy Q | Monotonic mixing hypernet conditioned on global state |
| VDN | Q-Learning-family ablation | Off-policy Q | Additive mixing, no hypernet |
| IQL | Q-Learning-family ablation | Off-policy Q | Independent learners, no mixing |

Mixed-radix policy: each algorithm's per-iteration actor sample budget is recorded but **not** normalized across algorithms; what is normalized is total env steps and total wall-clock, since the question is *training-time-to-score* not *iteration-efficiency*.

### 4.3 Pinned configs (U8)
- Source of truth: JaxMARL repository, path `algorithms/smax/{ippo,mappo,qmix,vdn,iql}/*.py` and any `config.yaml`/registry entries found alongside.
- **Action**: every config dict is **pinned verbatim** at the released commit hash specified at the top of the per-run overrides table. Any deviation (new optimizer, batch size change, etc.) is logged in **Table 9-Offline** (per-run overrides) with: deviation, rationale, expected effect, observed effect (to be filled at execution time only if execution is later authorized).

### 4.4 Networks, shared & differing components

**Shared**:
- 2-layer MLP body, 64 hidden units per layer, ReLU activation. **No GRU encoder** in the headline comparison.
- Observation, action, and global-state shapes as exposed by JaxMARl SMAX (intentionally identical for both arms).
- Identical reward function (JaxMARL SMAX default — sparse win/loss + shaped components; to be confirmed verbatim against the repo).
- Identical environment wrappers: `SMAXLogWrapper` and any defaults JaxMARL applies in its SMAX benchmark scripts.
- Identical eval wrapper and identical deterministic-eval policy (argmax for Q-Learning, mean for PPO).

**Differing (intentional, not "balanced")**:
- Optimizer hyperparameters (lr, clip ratio for PPO; target-update period, ε schedule for Q-Learning). Pinned from JaxMARL released configs.
- Rollout vs. replay data pipeline (on-policy buffer for PPO; replay buffer for Q-Learning).
- Critic head: V(s,τ) for MAPPO, V_i(o_i) for IPPO, IQL tabular head, VDN mixer(s;ϕ), QMIX mixer as hypernet on global state.

### 4.5 Optimization & rollout configurations
- Headline env-step budget per run: **2×10⁶**. PPO collects on-policy rollouts and discards; Q-Learning fills a replay buffer of JAX-prerelease default size and samples minibatches.
- Eval cadence: fixed to **(n_eval_episodes, eval_period_env_steps)** = **(32, 10⁴)** — i.e., 32 deterministic eval episodes every 10,000 env steps reported on the learning curve.
- Total checkpoints per run: ~200 (2×10⁶ / 10⁴).

### 4.6 Reward and normalization notes
- Reward signal follows JaxMARL default; **no per-algorithm shaping permitted** in headline runs.
- Evaluation policy for both arms is deterministic on the eval seed set.

### 4.7 Global state disclosure (per U7)
- The **QMIX mixer hypernetwork is allowed to access SMAX's global state** as in standard QMIX (Rashid et al.). This is **disclosed as an asymmetry** in the final report: MAPPO's centralized critic also uses global state, IPPO does not, VDN/IQL do not. Therefore the head-to-head QMIX-vs-MAPPO test is *symmetric* on global-state exploitation; the head-to-head against IPPO/VDN/IQL is *asymmetric in QMIX's favor* and is the reason those ablations exist as family-context, not as head-to-head.

---

## 5. Controls

### 5.1 Seeds (U3)
- Headline: **5 seeds per (algorithm × map)**, fixed seed set published in the design document.
- If any run exceeds a documented runtime threshold (declared in the design as "PLANNED BUDGET CAP, NOT MEASURED"), reduce it to **3 seeds** and add the run to a per-run **SeedFloorRunLog** table that records: which run fell to 3 seeds, what its actual wall-clock was, and which statistical-analysis pools it is excluded from.
- Eval seeds are a separate, published set and are *not* reused for training.

### 5.2 Hardware (U4)
- **One machine per campaign**; one JAX backend per run (`jax` with platform string pinned at run start), one process layout (no distributed).
- If a GPU is available: declare GPU model, VRAM, CUDA/cuDNN version, JAX build SHA. **Per-run metadata records `jax.devices()` and the platform string.**
- If only CPU: pin to the visible 24 vCPU budget, set `XLA_FLAGS` to disable thread pool oversubscription, and use `jax_platforms=cpu`.
- **No claim of measured wall-clock.** Runtime figures in §9 are *projected ranges*, explicitly unverified.

### 5.3 Eval protocol
- Fixed eval seed set of 32 seeds, distinct from training seeds.
- Deterministic policy (argmax for categorical Q-Learning; mean action for PPO stochastic policies).
- 32 episodes per checkpoint ⇒ confidence intervals reported with at least 32-sample normality-safe bootstrap.

### 5.4 Per-run overrides table headers
- **(run_id, map, algorithm, seed, train_env_steps, eval_seed_set, jax_backend, device_count, pinned_config_sha, deviations, jax_build_sha, run_started_utc, run_ended_utc, wallclock_seconds, normalized_score_final, AUC_env_steps, time_to_0p6, time_to_0p7, time_to_0p8)**.
- The "deviations" column is empty unless U8 forecloses-by-default; any non-empty entry triggers a per-deviation note.

---

## 6. Measurement protocols

### 6.1 Normalized score (per episode, per map)
- Compute **score_random** = mean ± 95% CI of episode return under a uniform-random policy over 32 eval seeds (per map).
- Compute **score_expert** as the larger of: (a) the JaxMARL paper's published best normalized score for that map, or (b) the best score achieved by **any** of our runs for that map (including un-run failures discounted). Apply *the same `score_expert`* to both PPO and QMIX (and ablations) — no asymmetric normalization is permitted.
- `normalized_score(τ) = (score(τ) − score_random) / (score_expert − score_random)`, clipped to [0, 1] for reporting (clipping only for display, not for statistical tests).
- `AUC_env_steps` = ∫ normalized_score d(env_step) / (final eval time × env_step_normalization).

### 6.2 Training-time metrics
- **Wall-clock seconds to first reach 0.8·*score_expert*** (primary): linear interpolation between the first checkpoint ≥ 0.8 and the immediately preceding checkpoint; interval mid-point reported as `time_to_0p8`.
- **Same for 0.6 and 0.7** (sensitivity sweep per U6); reported alongside.
- **Env steps to threshold** computed identically between the same two checkpoints; interval mid-point reported.
- **Per-step wall-clock** = total training wall-clock / total env steps (μs/env-step figure).
- **Total wall-clock to budget cap** — reported but not the primary metric.

### 6.3 Eval cadence & checkpoints
- Fixed: 32 episodes × every 10,000 env steps ⇒ ~200 checkpoints per headline run.
- An optional extension run exists per map at 5×10⁶ env steps for 3s_vs_5z/5m_vs_6m only (per U5). Checkpoint policy scales to match.

---

## 7. Statistical analysis plan (U9)

### 7.1 Per-map analysis
For each map and each metric M ∈ {final normalized score, env-steps-to-0.8, wallclock-to-0.8, AUC}:
- Compute per-seed scalar `M_{arm, s}`.
- Compute per-seed delta `ΔM_s = M_{MAPPO, s} − M_{QMIX, s}` (sign convention: positive Δ means MAPPO is better *in the metric's preferred direction*; direction is declared at the top of the results table).
- **Wilcoxon signed-rank test** on ΔM_s, exact permutation distribution when n=5 seeds.
- **Bootstrap CI**: 10,000 resamples of (run_id, not seed) with replacement; report 95% percentile interval; this is in addition to the Wilcoxon test, never a substitute.

### 7.2 Aggregate analysis
- Pool per-seed deltas across maps and run a Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap on the pooled set; declare stratification by map as a robustness check.
- Aggregate effect size: Hodges–Lehmann estimator at the pooled level.

### 7.3 Correction and reporting
- **Holm–Bonferroni** is applied across the family of headline metrics: {final normalized score, time-to-0.8, steps-to-0.8, AUC}. Each comparison reports (p_raw, p_adjusted, CI_95).
- Any *secondary* sensitivity-sweep metrics (time-to-0.6, time-to-0.7) are *not* included in the Holm family to avoid double-counting; they are reported as supplementary sweep without confirmatory language.

### 7.4 Reporting artifacts (U9)
- **One learning-curve figure per map per metric**: 3 maps × 2 metrics (normalized score vs env-step; wallclock-to-threshold bar plot) = 6 figures. Each curve is mean ± 95% bootstrap CI across seeds. Wallclock-to-threshold bar plot is one figure *per metric per map*, replicated.
- **One aggregate results table per metric**: rows = (algorithm × map), columns = (mean_estimate, 95% CI, Δ vs MAPPO if applicable, p_raw, p_adjusted).
- **One summary paragraph**: pre-registered indirect-effect summary, hypothesis-by-hypothesis yes/no/indeterminate, with explicit reveal of which SeedFloorRunLog entries limited power.

---

## 8. Ablations table

| Ablation | Variates | Held constant | What it identifies | Mandatory? |
|----------|----------|---------------|--------------------|------------|
| IPPO ↔ MAPPO | Centralized critic present/absent | Body, env, seeds, eval | Centralized-critic contribution to PPO (H4) | **Yes** |
| IQL ↔ VDN ↔ QMIX | Mixing mechanic (none / additive / monotonic-hypernet) | Body, env, seeds, eval | Credit-assignment contribution inside Q-Learning (H5) | **Yes** |
| GRU on/off (applied to both arms) | Recurrence | Body, env, seeds, eval, episode length | Sample-efficiency vs throughput trade-off and direct effect on headline (H6) | Optional, only if budget allows |
| Optional: state-stripped QMIX (U7) | Global-state access prohibited in mixer hypernet | Body, env, seeds, eval, hypernet architectural params untouched | Net state-conditioning contribution to QMIX | **Optional**, only "if space allows" per U7 |
| Optional: 5×10⁶ env-step extension on 3s_vs_5z & 5m_vs_6m (U5) | Env-step budget | All else | Plateau behavior on harder maps (H1 robustness) | Optional, gated on smoke test |
| Reward-shape sensitivity | Turn off shaped component for one map × MAPPO × QMIX | All else | Score fragility to reward signal | **Optional** |

---

## 9. Feasibility / cost estimate

> **All runtimes below are PROJECTED RANGES, NOT MEASURED. They are placeholders for budget planning only.**

### 9.1 Run matrix (headline)
Each row is a (algorithm × map) cell × 5 seeds ⇒ each cell = 5 runs.

| Map | MAPPO | QMIX | IPPO (abl.) | VDN (abl.) | IQL (abl.) | Cell subtotal |
|-----|-------|------|-------------|------------|------------|---------------|
| 3m | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
| 3s_vs_5z | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
| 5m_vs_6m | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
| **Total** | **15** | **15** | **15** | **15** | **15** | **75 runs** |

### 9.2 Per-run projected wall-clock envelope (2×10⁶ env steps)

| Backend | Map | Projected range per run (NOT MEASURED) |
|---------|-----|----------------------------------------|
| GPU (e.g., A100-40GB) | 3m | TBD_estimate_low .. TBD_estimate_high |
| GPU (e.g., A100-40GB) | 3s_vs_5z | TBD_estimate_low .. TBD_estimate_high |
| GPU (e.g., A100-40GB) | 5m_vs_6m | TBD_estimate_low .. TBD_estimate_high |
| CPU (24 vCPU, JAX CPU backend) | 3m | TBD_estimate_low_C .. TBD_estimate_high_C |
| CPU (24 vCPU, JAX CPU backend) | 3s_vs_5z | TBD_estimate_low_C .. TBD_estimate_high_C |
| CPU (24 vCPU, JAX CPU backend) | 5m_vs_6m | TBD_estimate_low_C .. TBD_estimate_high_C |

The actual placeholder numbers are *not* inserted here because the design brief explicitly forbids stating runtimes. **At execution time the implementer fills in TBD_estimate_* from a 30-minute smoke run on each (backend, map) combo before scaling to the full 5-seed matrix.**

### 9.3 Aggregate cost envelope (2×10⁶ step headline only)

- **Total headline runs**: 75.
- **Total headline env steps**: 75 × 2×10⁶ = 1.5×10⁸ env steps.
- **Total headline wall-clock**: 75 × "single-run projected range" ⇒ generated at execution time only.
- **Optional extensions**: ≤ +10 to +20 runs (5×10⁶-step extension on harder maps × 2 algorithms × 5 seeds, subject to budget).
- **Optional state-stripped QMIX** (U7): ≤ +9 runs.
- **Random-baseline runs**: 3 maps × 5 seeds × 32 episodes ⇒ negligible.

### 9.4 Compute environment (U4)
- One fixed machine per campaign; visible 24 vCPU.
- Run table records `jax_platforms` and `len(jax.devices())` per row.
- No multi-machine distributed training; no implicit scale-out.

### 9.5 Storage & logging footprint
- Per run: per-checkpoint eval return + per-episode normalized score + metadata ≈ low single-digit MB → aggregate of order GB; final storage footprint to be measured at execution, not claimed here.

---

## 10. Threats to validity

1. **Family asymmetry in CTDE access (U7).** QMIX and MAPPO both see global state during training; IPPO, VDN, IQL do not. Head-to-head comparisons of *asymmetric* pairs are biased in the global-state-accessor's favor. **Mitigation**: report the head-to-head PPO-vs-QMIX as the headline (symmetric), label any *cross-family* claim with this caveat, and log an optional state-stripped QMIX if budget allows.
2. **Hardware normalization (U4).** Wall-clock is only meaningful on a fixed backend with a fixed device count. **Mitigation**: env-step-to-threshold is the hardware-portable secondary metric; per-run metadata pins both `jax_platforms` and device count.
3. **Expert-score provenance.** Whether `score_expert` is JaxMARL-paper published or self-observed changes the absolute reading of normalized scores. **Mitigation**: declare which one, freeze the choice, apply identically to both arms, and report both normalized and raw return in the supplementary table.
4. **Hyperparameter pinning vs. re-tuning (U8).** Verbatim-pinned configs may favor one family if not jointly tuned. **Mitigation**: deviations table is mandatory and any deviation is conservatively treated as a known confound; no re-tuning in the headline comparison.
5. **Seed-floor collapses (U3).** If any run falls back from 5 to 3 seeds, power is materially reduced. **Mitigation**: SeedFloorRunLog names the affected runs; affected cells are excluded from headline Holm testing and reported with a power caveat.
6. **Curriculum / map difficulty ceiling.** On 5m_vs_6m, both algorithms may fail to reach 0.8·*score_expert* even at 5×10⁶ steps. **Mitigation**: report "did not reach" as a censored observation rather than capping; use Tobit-style interpolation on the time-to-threshold metric with explicit handling of non-events.
7. **GPU vs. CPU scaling discontinuity.** Some MARL implementations have non-monotonic throughput on CPU large-batch JIT. **Mitigation**: declare backend once, do not cross-compare CPU and GPU results.
8. **JAX non-determinism.** Despite `jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", False)` and seeded PRNGKeys, JAX's asynchronous dispatch and per-device ordering can introduce non-determinism. **Mitigation**: seed every PRNGKey explicitly, record `JAX_PRNG_KEYSET_SHA`, and report seed sensitivity in the supplementary appendix.
9. **Implementation version drift.** JaxMARL is under active development; minor API changes could break pinning. **Mitigation**: the pinned `algorithms/smax/{...}` SHA at the top of the overrides table is the single source of truth; deviations are the most-common expected event and are logged not hidden.
10. **Generalization beyond SMAX.** The same conclusion may not transfer to other JaxMARL environments (MPE, Overcooked, etc.). **Mitigation**: explicitly out of scope of this design and not claimed.

---

## 11. Reproducibility checklist

Every run produces a self-describing artifact. The header of each per-run log file must contain:

- [ ] `run_id` (unique)
- [ ] `algorithm` ∈ {MAPPO, IPPO, QMIX, VDN, IQL}
- [ ] `map` ∈ {3m, 3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m}
- [ ] `seed_train`, `seed_eval_set`
- [ ] `jax_version`, `jax_platforms`, `jaxlib_version`
- [ ] `cuda_version_if_any`, `libtpu_version_if_any`
- [ ] `devices_count`, `device_kind`
- [ ] `jax_pinned_config_sha`, `jaxmarl_repo_sha`, `jaxmarl_config_filename`
- [ ] `numpy_seed_root`, `python_hash_seed`
- [ ] `git_status_dirty` (bool), `docker_image_or_venv_spec_sha`
- [ ] `commit_message_of_pinned_config`
- [ ] Per-checkpoint: `(env_step, wallclock_seconds, eval_return, normalized_score, eval_seed_batch_id)`
- [ ] Per-run aggregate scalars: `final_normalized_score`, `AUC_env_steps`, `time_to_0p6`, `time_to_0p7`, `time_to_0p8` (each with "reached" boolean if censored)
- [ ] Empty `deviations` list if no overrides; otherwise per-deviation (replaced, by, reason, observed_directional_effect)
- [ ] `SeedFloorRunLog` flag if applicable (true ⇒ only 3 seeds; declares reduced statistical power)

A separate **campaign-level summary file** aggregates: campaign_id, machine_id (without PII), backend declaration, jaxmarl_repo_sha, list of run_ids, count of SeedFloor runs, count of deviated runs, count of censored time-to-threshold runs.

A **single summary paragraph** in the final report answers the four research questions:

1. Does MAPPO match QMIX in final normalized score on SMAX? *(H1 yes/no)*
2. Does QMIX reach 0.8·*score_expert* in fewer wall-clock seconds than MAPPO? *(H2 yes/no)*
3. Does QMIX do so in fewer environment steps? *(H3 yes/no)*
4. How much of the answer is attributable to (a) centralized critic, (b) mixing, (c) recurrence, (d) global-state access? *(H4–H6 filled)*

The final paragraph is reviewed against the SeedFloorRunLog and the deviations table **before publication** so any reduced-power or revised-hyperparameter caveat is in the same sentence as the claim it qualifies.

---

## Pre-registered lock-ins (re-statement for implementer hand-off)

- **Primary comparison arms**: MAPPO and QMIX.
- **Ablation arms**: IPPO, VDN, IQL.
- **Maps**: 3m, 3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m.
- **Headline seeds**: 5 (3 absolute floor under documented seed-floor policy).
- **Headline env-step budget**: 2×10⁶; optional 5×10⁶ on harder maps gated by smoke test.
- **Primary training-time metric**: wallclock-to-0.8·*score_expert*; sweep at 0.6/0.7/0.8.
- **Pinned JaxMARL configs**: `algorithms/smax/{ippo,mappo,qmix,vdn,iql}` verbatim.
- **Hardware**: one machine per campaign, one JAX backend, 24 vCPU visible, per-run metadata reports backend + device count.
- **No claim** of an executed experiment or measured runtime.
- **Statistical reporting**: Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap CI on per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX); Holm-Bonferroni across headline metrics; one learning-curve per (map, metric), one results table per metric, one summary paragraph.

disclosed_researcher_facts.text: Evaluate and compare PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) and Q-Learning for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in the SMAX (StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge in JAX) environment, focusing on training efficiency and performance.
JaxMARL, a JAX-based MARL library that enables large-scale parallelization and efficient GPU-accelerated training.
- SMAX: A JAX-based reimplementation of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC), designed for multi-agent micromanagement tasks.
